# Tiafoe qualifies for Nitto ATP Finals for first time

6 November 2026

By ATP Staff

Frances Tiafoe has qualified for the Nitto ATP Finals for the first time in his career.

Only one singles spot remains at the season finale

Frances Tiafoe will make his debut at the Nitto ATP Finals.

The 28-year-old is the seventh player to qualify for the season finale, which will take place in Turin from 15-22 November. The American clinched his spot on Friday when Ben Shelton defeated Tommy Paul at the Rolex Paris Masters.

Only one singles spot remains at Inalpi Arena. Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz, Ben Shelton, Medvedev, Flavio Cobolli and Arthur Fils have qualified. Tiafoe, Cobolli and Fils are all first-time qualifiers.

If Taylor Fritz defeats Alcaraz in the Paris quarter-finals, he will qualify for Turin. If not, Rafael Jodar will make his debut.

Tiafoe has enjoyed not only a resurgent season, but the best of his career. He won the title in Halle and also made finals in Cincinnati and Acapulco.

The Maryland native this year reached his second ATP Masters 1000 final, and both of them have come in Cincinnati in the past three years (2024 and 2026). Tiafoe earned three Top-15 wins at the event, where he defeated Learner Tien, Felix Auger-Aliassime and Lorenzo Musetti.

New York proved a happy hunting ground again for the home favourite, who reached the US Open semi-finals for the third time. Tiafoe upset 2021 champion and fellow Turin qualifier Daniil Medvedev en route to the last four. 

It is the second consecutive year in which two Americans have qualified for the Nitto ATP Finals after Shelton and Fritz last year. Before that, it had not happened since Andy Roddick and James Blake qualified in 2006.

# Jodar completes 2026 Nitto ATP Finals field

6 November 2026

By ATP Staff

Jodar qualifies year after competing in Next Gen ATP Finals

The field for the 2026 Nitto ATP Finals is now set.

After Carlos Alcaraz defeated Taylor Fritz on Friday in the Rolex Paris Masters quarter-finals, Rafael Jodar has qualified for the season finale, joining Alexander Zverev, Alcaraz, Ben Shelton, Daniil Medvedev, Flavio Cobolli, Arthur Fils and Frances Tiafoe in the field.

Zverev (2018 and 2021) and Medvedev (2020) are the two former Nitto ATP Finals singles champions set to compete in the year-end championships, which will take place in Turin from 15-22 November.

There will be four first-time competitors in the season finale: Cobolli, Fils, Tiafoe and Jodar. Zverev, the new World No. 1 in the PIF ATP Rankings, leads the way, having qualified for the ninth time.

Three members of the ATP No. 1 Club — Zverev, Alcaraz and Medvedev — will compete at Inalpi Arena. Every Nitto ATP Finals champion since 2020 is now a member of the No. 1 Club.

Jodar was a practice partner at the 2024 Next Gen ATP Finals, then qualified for the event in 2025. He is the first player to qualify for the Nitto ATP Finals the year after competing in the Next Gen ATP Finals since countryman Alcaraz did so in 2021 and 2022.

One year ago, Jodar was still a college student-athlete at the University of Virginia and the No. 166 player in the PIF ATP Rankings. Now he is set to compete in the ATP Tour's season finale.

Cobolli is the fourth active Italian to play on home soil in the season finale, joining Matteo Berrettini, Jannik Sinner and Lorenzo Musetti. It is the fourth consecutive year in which an Italian has qualified for the singles field in Turin.

Fils will be the first Frenchman to compete in the season finale since Gael Monfils in 2016. With Alcaraz and Jodar in the field, two Spaniards have directly qualified for the first time since 2015 (Rafael Nadal and David Ferrer).

Shelton will try to become the first lefty to win the Nitto ATP Finals title since John McEnroe in 1984. Shelton (University of Florida) and Jodar (University of Virginia) both played college tennis, making it the first edition since 2018 (Kevin Anderson and John Isner) in which two former college tennis players have qualified for the season finale.

Shelton and Tiafoe will try to become the first American to win the year-end championships since Pete Sampras in 1999.

DRAW CEREMONY
This will be the sixth edition of the Nitto ATP Finals in Turin. The draw is set to take place on Thursday 12 November at approximately 12:45 p.m. CET, following the pre-tournament press conference.

This year, the singles groups will be the John McEnroe Group and the Ivan Lendl Group. In doubles, there will be the Todd Woodbridge Group and the Mark Woodforde Group.

# Cobolli qualifies for Nitto ATP Finals for first time

3 November 2026

By ATP Staff

Flavio Cobolli has qualified for the Nitto ATP Finals for the first time in his career.

Three singles spots remain at the season finale

Flavio Cobolli has qualified for the Nitto ATP Finals for the first time.

The 24-year-old clinched his spot at the season finale, which will take place in Turin from 15-22 November, when Casper Ruud defeated Rafael Jodar at the Rolex Paris Masters on Tuesday evening.

Cobolli is the fourth active Italian to qualify for the Nitto ATP Finals, joining Jannik Sinner, Matteo Berrettini and Lorenzo Musetti. He will compete alongside new World No. 1 Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz, Ben Shelton, Daniil Medvedev and three more qualifiers still to be confirmed.

It has been a memorable season for Cobolli, who reached his first major final at Roland Garros and claimed an ATP 500 title in Acapulco.

After winning his first match of the season at the United Cup, Cobolli lost four consecutive matches. But since then, he has played the best tennis of his career.

The Italian has beaten the likes of Zverev and Medvedev this year. Other standout results include his runs to the Wimbledon quarter-finals, the Cincinnati semi-finals and the Munich final.

But his best result to date came at Roland Garros, where he became the third man born in the 2000s, after Alcaraz and Sinner, to compete in a major final.

The final three spots in the year-end championships will be decided this week in Paris at the final ATP Masters 1000 event of the season. Jodar is currently in the final qualifying position, but the likes of Alex de Minaur and Novak Djokovic have an opportunity to pass him.

Jodar has since surged to new heights in a standout 2026. The Spaniard won his maiden ATP Tour title in Marrakech, reached the quarter-finals at Roland Garros, and at ATP Masters 1000 events in Rome and Madrid.

If Jodar qualifies for the Nitto ATP Finals, he will be just the third player to have qualified for the season-end event the year after playing at the Next Gen ATP Finals. Stefanos Tsitsipas won the title in London in 2019 after triumphing in Milan in 2018, while Alcaraz qualified for the season finale in 2022 after winning the 20-and-under event in 2021.

Taylor Fritz has also increased his qualification hopes after winning the title in Washington. The American is up five places to 10th after lifting his first trophy of 2026.

The 28-year-old is trying to make his fourth appearance at the year-end event in Turin, where he advanced to the championship match in 2024. Fritz is part of a large group separated by just 375 points in the Live Race To Turin.

Record seven-time champion Novak Djokovic is sixth on 2,310 points, with Tommy Paul 14th on 1,935 points. Felix Auger-Aliassime, De Minaur, Fritz, Ben Shelton, Jodar, Jakub Mensik, Arthur Fils and Paul all head to the ATP Masters 1000 event in Montreal chasing points to boost their Nitto ATP Finals qualification chances.

Shelton and De Minaur both arrive off the back of quarter-final exits in Washington, while Auger-Aliassime will hope to ride home support to his first Masters 1000 crown. The hard-court event runs from 2-13 August, with Alexander Zverev and Auger-Aliassime the top two seeds.

Jannik Sinner has qualified for the Nitto ATP Finals, to be held from 15-22 November.
